code: # Example 1: globally stationary coefficients. # The diagnostics should usually not reject global adequacy or local # coefficient constancy because the response does not depend on location. set.seed(1) H <- simulate_H2(80, r_max = 3) Z <- H$Z x1 <- rnorm(80) x2 <- rnorm(80) y <- 1 + 2 * x1 - 0.5 * x2 + rnorm(80, sd = 0.3) dat <- data.frame(y, x1, x2)  fit_global <- lhwr(   y ~ x1 + x2,   data = dat,   Z = Z,   bw = 30,   adaptive = TRUE,   diagnostics = "aicc",   f_tests = TRUE ) fit_global$Ftests  # Example 2: hyperbolic coefficient heterogeneity. # The coefficients are generated from localized bumps defined by # Lorentz-hyperbolic distances, so the diagnostics may detect departures # from the global model and coefficient-specific local variability. set.seed(2) H <- simulate_H2(80, r_max = 3, uniform_area = TRUE) Z <- H$Z D <- hyperbolic_distance_matrix(Z, check = FALSE) x1 <- rnorm(80) x2 <- rnorm(80)  phi1 <- exp(-D[, 15]^2 / 0.7^2) phi2 <- exp(-D[, 45]^2 / 0.7^2) phi3 <- exp(-D[, 70]^2 / 0.7^2) beta0 <- 1 + 1.2 * phi1 beta1 <- 2 + 1.5 * phi2 beta2 <- -0.5 - 1.3 * phi3  eta <- beta0 + beta1 * x1 + beta2 * x2 y <- eta + rnorm(80, sd = 0.2) dat <- data.frame(y, x1, x2)  fit_local <- lhwr(   y ~ x1 + x2,   data = dat,   Z = Z,   bw = 25,   adaptive = TRUE,   diagnostics = "aicc",   f_tests = TRUE ) diagnostic_tests(fit_local)
